problem: This trap contradicts Section 2 and Worked Example 1. It says treating the inductor as an open circuit or the capacitor as a short at t = 0⁺ is wrong, and that the short/open rule belongs only to t → ∞ and DC steady state. But Section 2 and Step 3 of the worked example both use exactly that: with nothing stored, the 0 A inductor source is an open branch and the 0 V capacitor source is a short (20/4 = 5 A in Q6 depends on it). As written, a student who follows the trap will refuse to short the capacitor at 0⁺ and get the worked example and Q6 wrong.
fix: Reword: "Treating the inductor as an open circuit or the capacitor as a short at t = 0⁺ in every case. In general replace them by a current source i_L(0⁻) and a voltage source v_C(0⁻); they look like an open and a short only when nothing was stored (i_L(0⁻) = 0, v_C(0⁻) = 0). The unconditional short/open rule belongs to t → ∞ and the DC steady state."
